standard_prerequisites.name: Spreading an associated point to a neighbourhood, and the existence of a quasi-finite closed subscheme through a nearby point

standard_prerequisites.use: The first produces an open set on which generic points of fibres are associated points of the relative situation, the second gives an open subset of the base contained in the image of that open set, and the third cuts out a closed subscheme through the specialisation point which is quasi-finite there and meets the chosen open set away from the fibre over the base point.

core_obligations: Reduce to the locally finitely presented case with a closed specialisation point in the fibre, replace the source by the reduced structure on the closure of the first point, and set up the closure of the impurity point (proof lines 4707-4715).
Find the open set of associated points and an open subset of the base inside its image (proof lines 4716-4722).
Cut out the quasi-finite closed subscheme meeting that open set away from the special fibre and read off the required impurity (proof lines 4723-4729).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the locally finitely presented case (proof lines 4707-4715).
Get the open set of associated points and its open image in the base (proof lines 4716-4722).
Cut out the quasi-finite subscheme and conclude (proof lines 4723-4729).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that over a locally Noetherian base any impurity of a module above a point can be replaced by an impurity for which the morphism is quasi-finite at the specialisation point (statement lines 4698-4705, tag 05J1). The proof starts from the replacement impurity with a locally finitely presented morphism and a closed point of the fibre, reduces the source to a closure, uses three statements about associated points and quasi-finite subschemes to find an open set of associated points with an open image in the base and then to cut out a closed subscheme through the specialisation point which is quasi-finite there and meets that open set away from the special fibre, and reads off the impurity from a generic point of the resulting fibre. The chain of three geometric statements is the substance, so the claim is H2.
